legacy_root.answer: A marketplace registry entry is package_id = namespace/name with lowercase hyphenated identity, a versions[] list carrying channels, dependencies, compatibility, permissions, required provenance (artifact_sha256, source_uri, builder_id, built_at), signature, SBOM, license, vulnerability status, and quality score. Lifecycle is published|deprecated|revoked|deleted. Revoked versions stay in the index (presence=retained) with a revocation object so an already-installed client that refreshes can observe them; deleted versions are tombstones without a revocation object. Missing provenance is schema-invalid. This contract does not patch the live plugin-listing marketplace.schema.json. SUCCESS:ARC-0079

legacy_root.question: Specify the marketplace registry entry schema: package id and namespace rules, version list and channels, dependency metadata, platform and client compatibility, declared permissions, provenance, signature reference, SBOM reference, license metadata, vulnerability status, quality score, and the deprecation and revocation state machine - including how a revoked version is represented so an already-installed client can learn about it.

registry_entry_schema.description: One package record in the canonical registry index: identity, version list with channels, dependencies, compatibility, permissions, provenance, signature, SBOM, license, vulnerability status, quality score, and lifecycle. A revoked version stays in the index (presence=retained) so an already-installed client that refreshes can observe it. A deleted version is a tombstone without a revocation object. Absence of a row is not a revocation signal. SUCCESS:ARC-0079
registry_entry_schema.title: Marketplace registry index entry (ARC-0079)

x-revocation-vs-deletion.client_refresh: Installed clients learn revocation by matching package_id+version on a retained revoked row after index refresh, never by treating a missing row as revoked.
x-revocation-vs-deletion.deleted: lifecycle=deleted AND presence=tombstone AND tombstone object AND no revocation
x-revocation-vs-deletion.revoked: lifecycle=revoked AND presence=retained AND revocation object; row remains

already_installed_client.rule: A revoked version MUST remain in the index as a retained row (lifecycle=revoked, presence=retained, revocation populated). An already-installed client learns the revocation by refreshing the index and matching package_id+version on that retained row. Absence of a row, or a deleted tombstone, is not a revocation signal and MUST NOT be treated as one.

transitions.requires: tombstone object; presence=tombstone; no revocation object
tombstone object; presence=tombstone; no revocation object
